checklist.step: Monitor RMA release triggers and open an implementation intake for each
actions: Check the RMA website's Bulletins and Handbooks pages (Manager's Bulletins, Product Management Bulletins) and the Actuarial Information Browser each week for new releases affecting written states/crops.
Download the ADM release notice for the crop year and list the affected record categories (base rates, price elections, T-yields, dates, subsidy percentages, Special Provisions).
Open one ITSM intake per release, keyed by ADM version id and bulletin number, and attach the release notice.
Record the earliest sales closing date across affected crop/county cells as the hard deployment deadline on the intake.
checklist.done: every RMA release affecting written business has an ITSM intake carrying the ADM version id and its earliest sales closing date.

checklist.step: Download the ADM files and prove the download is complete
actions: Pull the full ADM dataset for the crop year from the RMA public download site (pubfs / Actuarial Data Master downloads) for every state/county/crop/plan combination the AIP writes.
Compare record counts per ADM table against the counts published in the RMA release layout/notice and resolve any difference before loading.
Compute and store file checksums, and archive the raw ADM files in a versioned staging area named <RY>-<ADM version>.
Notify the Pricing Actuary that the release is staged and control-totaled.
checklist.done: the raw ADM files are archived with checksums and record counts reconciled to the RMA release notice.

checklist.step: Verify form editions against FCIC form standards before configuration
actions: List every policy document touched by the release: Common Crop Insurance Policy Basic Provisions (7 CFR 457.8), crop provisions, Special Provisions, endorsements and AIP-created forms.
Compare each AIP-created form against the Document and Supplemental Standards Handbook (FCIC-24040) standards and record the FCIC edition date it must carry.
Reject any form whose text deviates from the FCIC-authorized wording — SRA Section IV(f)(1) allows no unapproved variation.
Write the authorized edition list onto the ITSM intake as the configuration target.
checklist.done: the intake carries a complete authorized-edition list traced to 7 CFR 457.8 and FCIC-24040.

checklist.step: Open the change record and set the release gate
actions: Convert the intake to a formal change record referencing the ADM version, bulletin numbers and authorized-edition list.
Back-schedule the plan: staging load, reconciliation, QA regression, actuarial sign-off, CAB approval, production deploy — all completing before the earliest sales closing date.
Set T-30/T-14/T-7 calendar alerts against that date.
Name the owner for each task and circulate the plan to the Pricing Actuary, QA Analyst and Policy Admin Ops Lead.
checklist.done: a scheduled change record exists with every task owned and dated ahead of the earliest sales closing date.

checklist.step: Load the ADM into the rating engine staging environment
actions: Map each ADM table (base rates, rate differentials, price elections/projected prices, transitional yields, subsidy factors, unit structure factors) to its rating-engine table.
Run the loader into staging and capture the load log with per-table row counts.
Reconcile loaded row counts to the archived ADM control totals; investigate any drop or duplicate.
Tag the staging configuration with the ADM version id so production can be traced to it later.
checklist.done: staging carries the full ADM release with load counts reconciled to the archived control totals.

checklist.step: Configure form editions and dates in the policy admin system
actions: Attach each authorized form edition to the affected plan/crop/state combinations with the correct crop-year effective date.
Expire the superseded editions so they cannot attach to new business after the contract change date.
Load the release's key dates (sales closing, acreage reporting, premium billing, end of insurance) into the policy calendar per the ADM dates records.
Print the configuration diff and attach it to the change record.
checklist.done: policy admin staging issues only authorized editions and carries the ADM key dates, with the diff attached to the change record.

checklist.step: Reconcile staged premium output to RMA expected values
actions: Build a test-case grid covering every written plan of insurance (YP, RP, RP-HPE, ARPI as applicable), representative counties, coverage levels 50-85%, and optional units vs enterprise units.
Price each test case in staging and independently in the RMA cost estimator / premium calculator using the same ADM version.
Compare premium, subsidy and producer premium per case at zero tolerance; log every difference as a defect.
File the reconciliation workpaper on the change record with the pass/fail per cell.
checklist.done: every test cell matches the RMA-derived premium exactly, or has an open defect blocking release.

checklist.step: Run the QA regression pack across plans and options
actions: Execute the FCIP regression suite: quote, bind, endorsement, acreage report and premium recompute flows for each plan and option combination.
Verify form packets render with the authorized edition footer on every page.
Verify superseded rates/editions are unreachable for the new crop year.
Log defects with severity; block release on any severity-1 rating or form defect.
checklist.done: the regression pack passes with no open severity-1 defects and form footers show authorized editions.

checklist.step: Capture actuarial sign-off on the rating implementation
actions: Review the reconciliation workpaper and defect log.
Sign a dated memo stating the staged rating matches ADM version <id> with zero premium differences.
Attach the memo to the change record — CAB may not approve without it.
checklist.done: a dated actuarial sign-off memo naming the ADM version is attached to the change record.

checklist.step: Take the release through change approval
actions: Present the change at CAB with the reconciliation, QA results, actuarial memo and the sales-closing-date deadline.
Record approver names and the approved deployment window in the change record.
Confirm a rollback plan exists that restores the prior ADM version and editions.
checklist.done: CAB approval, approvers and a tested rollback plan are recorded before deployment.

checklist.step: Deploy to production before the earliest sales closing date
actions: Execute the production deployment in the approved window.
Verify the production configuration tag matches the staged ADM version id.
Record deployment start/end timestamps in the change record.
Confirm the deployment date precedes the earliest sales closing date recorded on the intake.
checklist.done: production carries the tagged ADM version with a deployment timestamp ahead of the earliest sales closing date.

checklist.step: Validate production quotes post-deployment
actions: Re-run 20 of the reconciliation test cells directly in production.
Compare production premium, subsidy and producer premium to the staged and RMA-derived values.
Spot-check a bound policy's form packet for authorized edition footers.
Attach the production validation results to the change record.
checklist.done: production results match the RMA-derived values and form packets carry authorized editions.

checklist.step: Publish the release to agents and internal users
actions: Post the updated forms, key dates and plan availability to the agent portal.
Notify the distribution and underwriting teams of the contract change date and sales closing dates.
Point agents at the RMA bulletin for producer-facing changes.
checklist.done: agents can see the current editions and dates, and the notification is archived.

checklist.step: Close the change record with the full evidence set
actions: Attach the ADM control totals, reconciliation workpaper, QA results, actuarial memo, CAB approval and deployment timestamps.
Set the change record to Closed-Successful only when every artifact is present.
Cross-reference the change record id on the regulatory filing/issue tracker entry for the release.
checklist.done: the change record is closed with the complete evidence chain from RMA release to production validation.

checklist.step: Retain the system change evidence for the crop-year retention period
actions: Copy the closed change record package into the compliance evidence repository under <reinsurance year>/<ADM version>.
Apply the retention label: 3 years after the end of the crop year per 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 21, extended if FCIC issues a records notice.
Confirm the package is retrievable by ADM version, state and crop.
checklist.done: the implementation evidence is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by ADM version, state and crop.

testing.step: Build the population of FCIC releases and system changes for the reinsurance year
actions: Pull every ADM release and Manager's/Product Management bulletin for the reinsurance year from the RMA website affecting written states/crops.
Extract every policy admin and rating change record for the same period from the ITSM platform.
Join the two lists on ADM version/bulletin number so releases without a change record cannot hide.
testing.done: a joined population of RMA releases and system changes exists with no unmatched RMA release unexplained.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the RMA release index
actions: Compare the population against the RMA Actuarial Information Browser release history for each written state/crop.
List any RMA release with no corresponding deployment as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: every RMA release traces to a deployment or an exception, and the population is signed complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of releases introducing a new plan of insurance or new crop program.
Randomly select (seeded, reproducible) 25 state/county/crop/plan cells across the remaining releases.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all new-plan releases plus 25 random cells is documented.

testing.step: Independently recompute premium from the ADM for each sampled cell
actions: Download the ADM tables for the sampled cell directly from the RMA site — do not reuse the implementation team's staged files.
Price the cell in the RMA cost estimator / premium calculator at the sampled coverage level and unit structure.
Quote the identical cell in the production rating engine and compare premium, subsidy and producer premium at zero tolerance.
Record any difference as an exception with the differing field.
testing.done: every sampled cell's production premium matches the independently ADM-derived premium, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Trace production form editions to the FCIC-authorized editions
actions: Generate the form packet for a sampled policy in each sampled cell.
Compare each form number and edition footer to 7 CFR 457.8, the crop/Special Provisions and the FCIC-24040 authorized-edition list.
Treat any AIP-created form deviating from FCIC standards as a fail, not a formatting note.
testing.done: every sampled form packet carries only FCIC-authorized editions.

testing.step: Verify deployment beat the earliest sales closing date
actions: For each sampled release, read the production deployment timestamp from the change record.
Look up the earliest sales closing date for the affected cells in the ADM dates records.
Recompute the margin in days; any deployment on or after the sales closing date is an exception.
Check whether any business was quoted between the RMA release effective date and the deployment.
testing.done: every sampled release deployed before its earliest sales closing date, with quote-gap checks documented.

testing.step: Inspect change governance on the sampled releases
actions: Confirm each sampled change record holds the ADM control totals, reconciliation workpaper, QA results, actuarial sign-off memo and CAB approval.
Check the actuarial memo names the same ADM version as the production configuration tag.
Flag any release closed with missing artifacts.
testing.done: each sampled change record carries the complete, version-consistent evidence chain.

testing.step: Test the handling of any late or failed deployment
actions: Pull every release deployed late or rolled back during the year.
Verify each generated a logged exception identifying affected policies and whether any were written on stale rates or superseded forms.
Confirm affected policies were corrected and the correction evidenced.
testing.done: every late or failed deployment has a logged exception with the affected-policy analysis and correction evidence.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the ADM version, cell, what failed and the SRA Section IV(f)(1) impact.
Assign a root cause (missed bulletin, mapping defect, schedule crush, QA gap) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who performed none of the sampled implementations — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Run a single intake for all FCIC objections and rejections
actions: Check the designated RMA correspondence mailbox and the company's mail log every business day for FCIC/RMA letters, deficiency notices and findings.
Log in through USDA eAuthentication and pull the weekly eDAS edit/rejection report for every submitted batch.
Open one tracker item per notice or rejection batch within 1 business day of receipt, attaching the source document.
Record the notice date exactly as printed — the response clock runs from it.
checklist.done: every notice and rejection batch is in the tracker within 1 business day with its source attached and notice date captured.

checklist.step: Compute and record the response deadline on every item
actions: Read the notice for a stated deadline; where none is stated apply 45 days from the FCIC written notice date per the SRA.
For eDAS rejections, set the due date to the next weekly transaction cutoff date published in Appendix III.
Write due date, calculation basis and cite onto the tracker item.
Set T-20/T-10/T-3 reminders against the due date.
checklist.done: every open item shows a due date, the day-count basis and armed reminders.

checklist.step: Classify the objection and route it to the right owner
actions: Tag each item: Plan of Operations deficiency, form/procedure objection, data rejection, compliance finding, or premium/escrow discrepancy.
Assign the responding owner: Product Filing Specialist for forms, Data Quality Analyst for eDAS rejections, Regulatory Reporting Analyst for financial exhibits, Compliance Analyst for findings.
Notify the owner and the Compliance Manager of the assignment and due date the same day.
checklist.done: each item carries a classification, a named responding owner and a same-day notification.

checklist.step: Pull the requirement FCIC relied on and attach it
actions: Read the cited SRA section, appendix paragraph, handbook (e.g. LASH, FCIC-24040, Manual 14) or 7 CFR provision as currently in force.
Attach the cited text to the tracker item so the drafter answers the actual requirement.
Note any ambiguity for Regulatory Counsel before drafting starts.
checklist.done: the tracker item holds the current text of every requirement the notice cites.

checklist.step: Draft the response against each objection point
actions: Build a point-by-point response table: FCIC's objection, the company position, the corrective action, and the evidence attached.
Collect exhibits from the responding owner (corrected forms, revised Plan of Operations pages, reconciliations).
Where a correction needs more time, draft an extension request stating the reason and a committed date — submitted before the due date, never after.
Keep the draft in the tracker item with version history.
checklist.done: a point-by-point draft with exhibits (or a pre-deadline extension request) exists in the tracker item.

checklist.step: Correct and resubmit rejected data records by the weekly cutoff
actions: Open the eDAS edit report and group rejections by edit code and record type (policy, acreage, loss records per the Appendix III layouts).
Trace each rejected record to its source in the policy admin system and fix the source field, not just the extract.
Regenerate and resubmit the corrected batch through eDAS no later than the transaction cutoff date for the week.
Save the resubmission confirmation and the post-submission edit report showing the records accepted.
checklist.done: corrected records are accepted in eDAS by the weekly cutoff with confirmations saved to the tracker item.

checklist.step: Route the draft through counsel and compliance review
actions: Review every draft response for accuracy against the cited requirement and for admissions with SRA remedy exposure (Appendix IV sanctions).
Confirm any concession of a deficiency is factually supportable and paired with a corrective action.
Return edits within 5 business days of receiving the draft, leaving submission margin before the due date.
Stamp the approved version with name and date in the tracker item.
checklist.done: the response carries a dated counsel approval and no unreviewed admissions.

checklist.step: Submit the response through the channel the notice specifies
actions: Send the approved response to the address or RMA system the notice names (RMA regional compliance office, Deputy Administrator, or portal upload).
Capture proof of submission: portal confirmation id, delivery receipt or date-stamped transmittal letter.
Record the submission date on the tracker item and compare it to the due date.
File the as-sent package with all exhibits.
checklist.done: the response is submitted before the due date with proof of submission on the tracker item.

checklist.step: Track FCIC's disposition and any follow-up demand
actions: Monitor the mailbox for FCIC's acknowledgment, acceptance or follow-up interrogatory.
Open a linked tracker item for any follow-up with its own 45-day (or stated) deadline.
Chase RMA in writing if no disposition arrives within 60 days, and log the chase.
checklist.done: every submitted response shows an FCIC disposition or a logged, dated chase.

checklist.step: Escalate items at risk of missing the deadline
actions: Review the tracker at each T-10 alert and challenge whether the response will land on time.
For at-risk items, either compress the plan or have the extension request sent that day.
Escalate any item still unresolved at T-3 to the Head of Compliance with a written options note.
checklist.done: no item passes T-3 without a submitted response, a filed extension request, or a Head-of-Compliance decision.

checklist.step: Hold the weekly aging review
actions: Run the open-items report sorted by days-to-due and days-open.
Confirm every item has a current owner, next action and date.
Minute the review and any reassignments.
checklist.done: a minuted weekly review shows every open item owned with a dated next action.

checklist.step: File Plan of Operations amendments arising from objections
actions: Where the resolution changes the Plan of Operations (fund designations, forms list, financial exhibits), prepare the amendment pages.
Submit the amendment to RMA by the date set in the deficiency notice, keeping the April 1 annual filing cycle in view.
Link the amendment submission receipt to the originating tracker item.
checklist.done: every objection-driven Plan of Operations change is amended, submitted on time and linked to its objection.

checklist.step: Root-cause recurring objections and rejections
actions: Quarterly, pivot the tracker by objection type and eDAS edit code.
For any code recurring 3+ times, open a corrective action naming the process or system fix and its owner.
Track the corrective action to closure and check the recurrence stops.
checklist.done: recurring objection/edit codes each have an owned corrective action with closure evidence.

checklist.step: Close the tracker item with full disposition
actions: Record FCIC's final disposition and the dates: notice, due, submitted, disposed.
Confirm the item holds notice, requirement text, approved response, receipt and disposition before closing.
Mark late items Closed-Exception, never Closed-Complete.
checklist.done: closed items carry the complete correspondence chain and honest late/on-time status.

checklist.step: Retain the correspondence set for the retention period
actions: Move each closed item's package into the document management repository under <reinsurance year>/FCIC-correspondence.
Apply the 3-years-after-crop-year retention label with extension on FCIC notice.
Verify retrievability by notice date, objection type and disposition.
checklist.done: every closed objection package is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of notices and rejections for the quarter
actions: Export the RMA correspondence mailbox and the company mail log for the quarter and list every FCIC/RMA notice, objection and finding.
Pull every weekly eDAS edit/rejection report for the quarter via USDA eAuthentication.
Merge into one population keyed by notice date / batch week.
testing.done: a merged population of all notices and rejection batches for the quarter exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the tracker to the source population
actions: Match every population row to a tracker item on notice date and subject.
List any notice or rejection batch with no tracker item as an automatic exception — unlogged notices are the highest-risk failure.
Check logging happened within 1 business day of receipt for matched items.
testing.done: every notice and rejection batch matches a tracker item logged within 1 business day, or is an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of Plan of Operations deficiency notices and compliance findings.
Randomly select (seeded, reproducible) 15 further items including at least 4 eDAS rejection batches.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all deficiency notices plus 15 random items is documented.

testing.step: Recompute every sampled deadline and compare to the actual response date
actions: Recompute the due date from the printed notice date: stated deadline, else 45 days; for rejections, the next weekly transaction cutoff date.
Compare the recomputed due date to the tracker's due date and to the proof-of-submission date.
Any response after the recomputed due date without a pre-deadline extension request is a fail.
Record the day-count maths per item in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled item has independent day-count maths and an on-time/late verdict.

testing.step: Assess whether each sampled response actually answered the objection
actions: Re-read the notice's cited requirement (SRA section, handbook, 7 CFR) as of the notice date.
Check the response addressed every objection point with evidence, not restatement.
Flag any response that conceded a deficiency without a corrective action or counsel stamp.
testing.done: each sampled response is judged responsive point-by-point, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace proof of submission and FCIC disposition
actions: Verify each sampled item holds a portal confirmation id, delivery receipt or date-stamped transmittal.
Verify the disposition (or a dated chase after 60 days) is recorded.
Treat a response with no submission proof as unsubmitted — a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled response traces to dated submission proof and a disposition or chase.

testing.step: Verify rejected data cleared eDAS on resubmission
actions: For sampled rejection batches, open the post-resubmission eDAS edit report.
Confirm the previously rejected records show accepted status by the committed cutoff week.
Check the fix was made in the policy admin source, not only in the extract, by inspecting the source field.
testing.done: sampled rejected records show accepted status in eDAS with source-level fixes evidenced.

testing.step: Test that escalations fired for at-risk items
actions: For sampled items that came within 10 days of their due date, verify the T-10 alert reached the Compliance Manager.
For any that reached T-3 unresolved, verify the Head-of-Compliance escalation note exists.
Verify extension requests were submitted before, not after, the due date.
testing.done: escalation and extension evidence exists for every sampled at-risk item.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with notice reference, what failed and the SRA exposure.
Assign root cause (intake miss, day-count error, SME delay, submission channel confusion) and an owner.
Set remediation dates and carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the late-response rate against the zero-late threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who drafted none of the sampled responses — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and late-response rate is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Define the archive taxonomy and index standard
actions: Create the folder taxonomy: <reinsurance year>/<writing company>/<document class> with classes for Plan of Operations, FCIC approvals, forms & conformity evidence, eDAS confirmations, correspondence.
Define mandatory metadata per item: reinsurance year, state, crop (where applicable), document class, receipt date, source, retention date.
Publish the standard to everyone who files FCIC documents and lock the taxonomy against ad-hoc folders.
checklist.done: the taxonomy and metadata standard is published and enforced in the repository.

checklist.step: Capture the Plan of Operations as-filed package every year
actions: Obtain from the Regulatory Filing Specialist the complete package submitted to RMA by April 1: financial exhibits, projected premium by state and fund, forms list, and the transmittal.
File it under <reinsurance year>/Plan of Operations with the submission receipt.
Diff the package against the tracker's submission record to confirm nothing filed is missing from the archive.
checklist.done: each reinsurance year holds the complete as-filed Plan of Operations package with its receipt.

checklist.step: Capture every FCIC approval letter and disposition
actions: Collect the FCIC approval of the Plan of Operations (issued ahead of the July 1 reinsurance year start) and any conditional-approval terms.
Collect approval or objection dispositions for amendments, AIP-created forms and procedure submissions.
File each within 5 business days of receipt, linked to the filing it approves.
checklist.done: every filed item is linked to its FCIC approval or disposition, filed within the 5-day SLA.

checklist.step: Archive form editions with their conformity evidence
actions: For each crop year, deposit the authorized form editions used (Basic Provisions, crop provisions, Special Provisions, AIP-created forms).
Attach the FCIC-24040 conformity check and the edition-date inventory produced during implementation.
Link each form record to the policy admin configuration change record that deployed it.
checklist.done: each crop year's form set is archived with conformity evidence and a link to its deployment record.

checklist.step: Archive eDAS submission confirmations and settlement correspondence
actions: Save the weekly eDAS acceptance confirmations and the monthly settlement/escrow correspondence with RMA.
File by reinsurance year and submission week so a given week's acceptance can be produced on demand.
Flag any week with no confirmation on file to the Regulatory Filing Specialist the same day.
checklist.done: every submission week shows an acceptance confirmation on file or a same-day flag.

checklist.step: Maintain version linkage between filed, approved and implemented versions
actions: For every document class, link the as-filed version, the FCIC-approved version (with conditions) and the implemented version in production.
Where the approved version differs from the filed version, store both and mark the delta.
Never overwrite — supersede with a new version and keep the chain.
checklist.done: any filing can be walked filed → approved → implemented with no overwritten versions.

checklist.step: Apply retention labels at intake
actions: Set the retention date at intake: 3 years after the end of the applicable crop year per 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 21.
Extend the date on any FCIC records-retention notice, and record the notice as the reason.
Set Plan of Operations approvals to life-of-relationship plus 3 years.
checklist.done: every archived item carries a computed retention date with its basis.

checklist.step: Restrict write access and log every change
actions: Grant read access to compliance, filing and audit staff; restrict write/delete to named records staff.
Enable the repository audit trail on the archive folders.
Review the access list quarterly with the Access Management Analyst and remove leavers.
checklist.done: write access is limited to named records staff, audited, and reviewed quarterly.

checklist.step: Enforce the 5-business-day intake SLA
actions: Run the intake queue daily; anything received but unfiled at day 3 gets a reminder, at day 5 an escalation to the Compliance Manager.
Record receipt date vs filed date on every item.
Report SLA performance monthly.
checklist.done: intake SLA performance is measured and no item sits unfiled past 5 business days without escalation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive to the filing calendar quarterly
actions: Build the expected-item list for the quarter from the filing calendar, the tracker and the eDAS submission history.
Check each expected item exists in the archive with complete metadata.
Log every gap as an exception and open a re-request to RMA or an internal reconstruction task.
checklist.done: a quarterly reconciliation shows every expected item present or excepted with an owner.

checklist.step: Integrate legal holds
actions: On any litigation, arbitration or FCIC compliance investigation, issue a hold naming the affected reinsurance years and document classes.
Have the Records Manager suspend disposal on held items in the repository.
Release holds in writing and re-apply standard retention on release.
checklist.done: holds suspend disposal on named items and are released only in writing.

checklist.step: Run integrity checks on stored files
actions: Verify checksums on a rotating sample of archived files each quarter.
On any format migration, re-verify checksums and re-run a render check on migrated documents.
Log integrity failures as exceptions with the affected items.
checklist.done: quarterly integrity checks pass or every failure is an owned exception.

checklist.step: Run the annual retrieval drill
actions: Before July 1, have the Compliance Manager name 10 items across years and classes without warning.
Retrieve each with its approval linkage within 1 business day.
Record retrieval times and misses in the drill log.
checklist.done: 10 named items are produced within 1 business day, with times logged.

checklist.step: Log and disposition archive exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every missing item, integrity failure or failed retrieval.
Assign root cause (never received, misfiled, over-deleted, migration loss) and an owner.
Close only when the item is recovered, re-requested from RMA, or formally accepted as irrecoverable by the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every archive exception has an issue, root cause, owner and an evidenced disposition.

checklist.step: Review and re-approve the archive procedure annually
actions: Re-read the SRA record terms and 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 21 for retention changes before the April 1 filing cycle.
Update the procedure for any new document class (new plans of insurance, new RMA submission channels).
Sign and date the re-approval.
checklist.done: a dated annual re-approval exists reflecting current SRA and CFR retention terms.

testing.step: Build the expected-record population for two reinsurance years
actions: From the filing calendar, tracker and eDAS submission history, list every filing, approval and correspondence item expected for the current and one prior reinsurance year.
Include the Plan of Operations packages, FCIC approvals, form conformity sets and weekly confirmations.
Sign the expected list as complete before sampling.
testing.done: a signed expected-item list exists for both reinsurance years.

testing.step: Reconcile the archive index to the expected list
actions: Match every expected item to an archive entry with complete metadata.
List unmatched expected items as exceptions; list archive entries matching nothing as misfiles to investigate.
Compute the completeness percentage against the 98% threshold.
testing.done: a completeness percentage is computed with every gap and misfile listed.

testing.step: Draw the retrieval sample
actions: Take 100% of Plan of Operations packages and their FCIC approval letters for both years.
Randomly select (seeded, reproducible) 20 further items across classes, including at least 4 weekly eDAS confirmations and 4 form conformity sets.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample including all Plan of Operations packages is documented.

testing.step: Retrieve and inspect each sampled item for completeness
actions: Retrieve each sampled item and time the retrieval.
Verify the package is complete: filed version, approval/disposition, receipt, and metadata populated.
Verify documents render and match their checksums.
testing.done: every sampled item is retrieved, timed, complete and readable, or the failure is logged.

testing.step: Trace archived filed versions to what production actually implemented
actions: For sampled form sets, compare the archived approved edition dates to the editions configured in the policy admin system for that crop year.
Any production edition not matching an archived approved version is an exception feeding the C49 implementation test.
Record the trace per sampled form.
testing.done: sampled archived editions match production configuration or the mismatch is escalated.

testing.step: Test retention labels and the disposal log
actions: Recompute the retention date for each sampled item from its crop year and compare to the label.
Inspect the disposal log for the period and verify nothing inside its retention period or under hold was destroyed.
Verify FCIC extension notices, where issued, moved the affected labels.
testing.done: retention labels recompute correctly and the disposal log shows no premature destruction.

testing.step: Review access rights and the audit trail
actions: Pull the current access list and verify write/delete is limited to named records staff.
Check the quarterly access reviews happened and leavers were removed.
Sample the audit trail for one sampled item and verify changes trace to authorized users.
testing.done: access is appropriately restricted, reviewed quarterly, and the audit trail is intact.

testing.step: Verify the quarterly reconciliations and annual drill ran
actions: Inspect the four quarterly reconciliation workpapers and the annual retrieval drill log for the year.
Verify exceptions raised there were tracked to disposition.
Re-perform one quarter's reconciliation on a spot-check basis.
testing.done: all four reconciliations and the drill are evidenced with exceptions dispositioned.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the item, year, class and what is missing or wrong.
Assign root cause (intake miss, misfile, deletion, migration loss) and an owner.
Set remediation dates; missing FCIC approvals trigger a written re-request to RMA.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare completeness and retrieval results to the 98% / zero-critical-miss thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who administers nothing in the repository — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and completeness rate is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain the documented capital methodology
actions: Re-read SRA Appendix II each reinsurance year and update the methodology for changed fund terms, cession rates or reporting requirements.
Document every input source, formula and judgement (fund mapping, premium recognition point, reinsurance treatment).
Version the methodology and record CFO/Head of Capital Management approval.
checklist.done: a current, approved methodology reflecting this reinsurance year's SRA terms exists under version control.

checklist.step: Pull quarter-end statutory surplus and tie it out
actions: Extract policyholder surplus from the quarterly statutory statement (Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds page).
Tie the figure to the SAP S/4HANA GL equity accounts and to the prior quarter's roll-forward.
Document the tie-out with the extract date and preparer.
checklist.done: surplus is extracted and tied to both the statutory statement and the GL with a documented tie-out.

checklist.step: Extract MPCI premium by state and fund from reported data
actions: Pull net book premium by state, crop and fund designation from the warehouse tables fed by the weekly eDAS submissions.
Reconcile the total to the latest eDAS-accepted cumulative premium for the reinsurance year.
Flag any state where premium is still loading (late acreage reports) and note the estimation basis.
checklist.done: premium by state and fund reconciles to eDAS-accepted totals with estimation bases noted.

checklist.step: Apply the fund designations from the approved Plan of Operations
actions: Load the Assigned Risk Fund and Commercial Fund designations and retained percentages by state exactly as approved in the current Plan of Operations.
Verify no policy-level designation in the data contradicts the approved plan.
Record the Plan of Operations version and approval date used.
checklist.done: fund designations in the calc match the approved Plan of Operations version cited in the workbook.

checklist.step: Compute FCIC cessions and net retained premium
actions: Apply the SRA quota-share cession to FCIC per fund and state to derive company-retained premium.
Apply the Appendix II gain/loss sharing structure to understand retained underwriting exposure by fund.
Summarize retained premium by fund, state and total in the capital workbook.
checklist.done: retained premium is computed per fund and state using the current SRA terms, summarized in the workbook.

checklist.step: Overlay private reinsurance protection
actions: Pull the executed private stop-loss/quota-share treaties covering the MPCI book from the treaty repository.
Confirm inception dates, layers, co-participations and any SRA-related warranties against the signed contracts.
Model the net position after private protection and record treaty references in the workbook.
checklist.done: the net retained position reflects executed private treaties with contract references recorded.

checklist.step: Compute the retained-premium-to-surplus measure and headroom
actions: Compute retained MPCI premium relative to statutory surplus and compare against the premium volume the surplus supports under the Appendix II standards and the authorization in the approved Plan of Operations.
Express headroom in dollars and percentage against the authorized maximum.
Chart the quarter-on-quarter trend for the CFO pack.
checklist.done: the quarter's ratio, authorized maximum and headroom are computed and trended.

checklist.step: Roll forward the NAIC RBC position
actions: Annually, take the filed RBC (from the annual statement filing) as the anchor; quarterly, estimate movements from premium growth, reserve changes and investment mix.
Compare the estimated RBC ratio to the company action level and the internal buffer.
Note crop concentration effects on R5 premium risk in the commentary.
checklist.done: an RBC position (filed or estimated) with buffer comparison accompanies each quarterly calc.

checklist.step: Reconcile every input before results are used
actions: Tie surplus to the statutory statement, premium to eDAS-accepted totals, and reinsurance terms to executed treaties.
Clear every reconciling item above the documented threshold before sign-off.
File the reconciliation tab in the workbook.
checklist.done: all three input reconciliations are clean or every break is explained and accepted in writing.

checklist.step: Peer-review the calculation
actions: Have an actuary who did not prepare the quarter's workbook re-trace formulas, fund mappings and treaty terms.
Check formula integrity against the prior quarter's version (no silent changes).
Record reviewer name, date and findings in the workbook sign-off tab.
checklist.done: a documented peer review by a non-preparer is recorded with findings cleared.

checklist.step: Document assumptions and limitations
actions: List estimation points (in-flight acreage, loss development, prevented-planting uncertainty) and their direction of risk.
State the sensitivity of headroom to the top three assumptions.
Attach the note to the CFO pack.
checklist.done: an assumptions-and-limitations note with sensitivities accompanies the results.

checklist.step: Present results to the CFO and Head of Capital Management
actions: Deliver the quarterly pack: ratio, headroom, RBC position, trend and assumptions within 30 days of quarter close.
Record decisions (e.g. buy additional private cover, request authorization change) with owners.
Minute the review.
checklist.done: a minuted quarterly review with decisions and owners exists within 30 days of close.

checklist.step: Feed the calc into the Plan of Operations premium authorization
actions: Provide the Regulatory Reporting Manager the surplus-supported premium figure for the Plan of Operations due to RMA by April 1.
Reconcile the requested authorization to the latest calc and to growth plans.
Keep the derivation linking calc to request in the workbook.
checklist.done: the April 1 authorization request traces arithmetically to the capital calc.

checklist.step: Log breaches and calc exceptions
actions: Log any quarter where retained premium approaches or exceeds the authorized/supported level, any late calc, and any material input break.
Trigger the C53 escalation protocol for genuine breaches the same day.
Record disposition and CFO sign-off.
checklist.done: every breach or exception is logged with same-day escalation where required and CFO-signed disposition.

checklist.step: Archive the quarterly workbook and evidence
actions: File the locked workbook, input extracts, reconciliations, peer review and minutes under <reinsurance year>/<quarter>.
Apply the 3-years-after-crop-year retention label.
Verify retrievability by quarter.
checklist.done: each quarter's complete calc package is archived, labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of capital calcs and inputs for the year
actions: List the four quarterly calc packages, the annual RBC filing and the April 1 authorization derivation from the archive.
Confirm each expected package exists; a missing quarter is an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete.
testing.done: all expected calc packages are located or excepted, and the population is signed.

testing.step: Reconcile sampled inputs to source systems
actions: Independently re-extract surplus from the quarterly statutory statement and premium from the eDAS-accepted totals for two quarters.
Compare to the workbook inputs at zero tolerance.
Verify treaty terms in the workbook against the executed contracts in the treaty repository.
testing.done: sampled inputs match statutory, eDAS and treaty sources exactly, or breaks are logged.

testing.step: Re-perform one full quarterly calculation
actions: Rebuild the selected quarter's calc from the raw inputs without reference to the preparer's workbook.
Apply the approved methodology: fund designations, FCIC cessions, private overlay, ratio and headroom.
Compare the recomputed ratio and headroom to the reported figures within rounding.
Document every difference with its cause.
testing.done: an independent re-performance matches the reported ratio and headroom, or differences are causally explained.

testing.step: Trace fund designations to the approved Plan of Operations
actions: Open the FCIC-approved Plan of Operations for the reinsurance year from the filing archive.
Compare the workbook's fund designations and retained percentages by state to the approved plan.
Any deviation is an exception regardless of direction.
testing.done: workbook fund terms match the approved Plan of Operations state by state.

testing.step: Verify the SRA terms applied are the current year's
actions: Compare the cession and gain/loss sharing parameters in the workbook to the executed 2026 SRA and its appendices.
Check no prior-year parameter survived the annual roll.
Record the comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: every SRA parameter in the calc matches the executed current-year agreement.

testing.step: Recompute the RBC linkage
actions: Tie the anchor RBC figures to the filed annual statement RBC pages.
Re-derive one quarterly RBC estimate from the stated movement drivers.
Check the buffer comparison used the current company action level.
testing.done: RBC anchors tie to the filing and the sampled estimate re-derives within tolerance.

testing.step: Verify governance on each quarter
actions: Check each quarter shows a non-preparer peer review, an assumptions note, minutes of the CFO review, and completion within 30 days of close.
Verify the April 1 authorization request traces to the calc.
Flag any quarter missing an element.
testing.done: all four quarters evidence peer review, CFO review, timeliness and the authorization trace.

testing.step: Test breach detection with a challenge scenario
actions: Inject a hypothetical premium uplift that would breach the authorized level into a copy of the workbook.
Verify the workbook flags the breach and the documented escalation path (C53) would trigger.
Record the challenge result.
testing.done: the challenge scenario demonstrably triggers the breach flag and escalation path.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with quarter, input and impact on the reported headroom.
Assign root cause (stale SRA parameter, tie-out miss, formula drift, late close) and an owner.
Set remediation dates; a misstated headroom triggers CFO notification the same day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, and same-day CFO notice where headroom was misstated.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare results to the zero-tie-out-break and rounding-match thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Model Risk Manager — who prepared none of the year's calcs — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper and report to the Compliance Committee and CFO.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee and CFO.

checklist.step: Define and approve the intervention ladder
actions: Set the ladder: internal early-warning buffer above the Appendix II surplus-supported premium level, the authorized premium level itself, and the NAIC RBC company/regulatory action levels.
Define for each rung: the metric, the trigger value, the required action and the escalation clock.
Obtain CFO approval and board risk committee ratification before July 1 each reinsurance year.
checklist.done: an approved ladder with metrics, triggers, actions and clocks exists for the current reinsurance year.

checklist.step: Automate the data feeds behind the monitoring metrics
actions: Build feeds from the GL and statutory reporting extracts into the Power BI capital dashboard: surplus, retained MPCI premium, RBC estimate, liquidity.
Refresh monthly at minimum and weekly during June-October as acreage and premium load through eDAS.
Alert the Capital Management Manager on any failed refresh the same day.
checklist.done: dashboard metrics refresh on schedule with failed refreshes alerted same day.

checklist.step: Produce the monthly monitoring pack by workday 10
actions: Compile surplus, retained premium vs authorization, headroom, RBC estimate and trend charts from the dashboard.
Annotate drivers: premium growth by state, loss emergence, investment movements.
Issue the pack to the CFO, Head of Capital Management and Chief Risk Officer by workday 10.
checklist.done: a dated pack with metrics, headroom and driver commentary is issued by workday 10 each month.

checklist.step: Track in-season retained exposure against capital
actions: During the growing season, update retained exposure weekly as acreage reports flow through eDAS submissions.
Project season-end retained premium and compare to the Plan of Operations authorization.
Flag to the CFO any projection that erodes the early-warning buffer.
checklist.done: weekly in-season projections exist June-October with buffer erosion flagged to the CFO.

checklist.step: Configure threshold alerts on every ladder rung
actions: Create an alert rule per rung routing to the Capital Management Manager and CFO office.
Test each rule quarterly by injecting a synthetic breach value in a non-production workspace.
Log the test results with dates.
checklist.done: every rung has a routed alert rule with quarterly synthetic tests logged.

checklist.step: Hold the monthly capital review
actions: Review the pack with the Capital Management Manager and Chief Risk Officer.
Decide actions on any amber metric and record owners and dates.
Minute the review and file the minutes with the pack.
checklist.done: a minuted monthly review with owned actions exists for every month.

checklist.step: Run the breach escalation protocol
actions: On any early-warning breach, open a GRC breach record and brief the CFO within 1 business day with the metric, cause and projection.
On any determination of a material adverse change in financial condition, start the 3-business-day clock for written notice to FCIC.
Record every timestamp — detection, CFO briefing, determination, notification — in the breach record.
checklist.done: every breach shows a timestamped chain from detection to CFO briefing (1 day) and, where required, FCIC notice (3 days).

checklist.step: Send the FCIC notification when triggered
actions: Draft the written notice to RMA describing the event, quantified impact on surplus and the management response.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the text and the CFO approve it.
Deliver to the RMA contact named in the SRA within 3 business days of the determination and capture proof of delivery.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared, CFO-approved notice reached RMA within 3 business days with delivery proof filed.

checklist.step: Maintain the management action playbook
actions: Keep pre-agreed actions current: additional private stop-loss purchase, capital injection from the parent, reduction of the requested premium authorization, cession plan changes.
For each action record trigger conditions, execution lead time and approvers.
Review the playbook annually alongside the ladder.
checklist.done: a current playbook with triggers, lead times and approvers accompanies the ladder.

checklist.step: Report to the board risk committee quarterly
actions: Present the capital position, headroom trend, breaches and actions via the board portal pack.
Record committee challenges and directions in the minutes.
File the pack and minutes in the archive.
checklist.done: quarterly board reporting with minutes exists for every quarter.

checklist.step: Track remediation actions to closure
actions: Track each breach action to its committed date in the GRC platform.
Verify the metric returned above the trigger and attach the evidencing pack.
Obtain CFO closure sign-off.
checklist.done: every breach action is closed with metric-recovery evidence and CFO sign-off.

checklist.step: Review thresholds annually
actions: Before July 1, re-derive the ladder from the new SRA terms, the new Plan of Operations authorization and updated RBC parameters.
Document what changed and why.
Re-obtain CFO and board risk committee approval.
checklist.done: a re-approved ladder aligned to the new reinsurance year exists before July 1.

checklist.step: Validate metric derivations annually
actions: Re-derive each dashboard metric from source for one month and compare to the displayed value.
Fix any transformation defect found and re-run.
Document the validation in the model file.
checklist.done: an annual validation shows dashboard metrics re-derive from source within rounding.

checklist.step: Coordinate monitoring outputs with regulatory reporting
actions: Cross-check that any breach disclosed to FCIC is consistently reflected in the quarterly financial submission to RMA (within 45 days) and statutory filings.
Reconcile figures quoted in notices to the monitoring pack of record.
Log any inconsistency as an exception before submission.
checklist.done: notices, RMA submissions and packs quote consistent figures, or the inconsistency is excepted pre-submission.

checklist.step: Retain monitoring evidence
actions: File packs, minutes, alert logs, breach records and FCIC notices under <reinsurance year>/capital-monitoring.
Apply the 3-years-after-crop-year retention label.
Verify retrievability by month and by breach.
checklist.done: the full year's monitoring evidence is archived, labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Inventory the year's monitoring packs and breach records
actions: List the twelve expected monthly packs, the weekly in-season projections and every GRC breach record for the year.
A missing month or missing in-season week during June-October is an automatic exception.
Sign the inventory as complete.
testing.done: a signed inventory shows every expected pack and projection present or excepted.

testing.step: Re-derive the monitored metrics for sampled months
actions: For three sampled months, independently recompute surplus, retained premium vs authorization and headroom from statutory extracts and eDAS-accepted premium.
Compare to the pack values within rounding.
Trace the authorization figure to the FCIC-approved Plan of Operations.
testing.done: sampled pack metrics re-derive from source and the authorization traces to the approved plan.

testing.step: Test the alert configuration end to end
actions: Inspect each ladder rung's alert rule: metric, trigger value and recipients against the approved ladder.
Review the quarterly synthetic-breach test logs for all four quarters.
Have one synthetic breach re-run in the test workspace and observe the alert arrive.
testing.done: alert rules match the approved ladder and a live synthetic test delivered the alert.

testing.step: Recompute the escalation timeline for every breach
actions: For each breach record, read the detection, CFO-briefing, determination and notification timestamps.
Recompute business-day counts: CFO within 1 business day; FCIC notice within 3 business days of a material-adverse-change determination.
Any late step is a fail; an undetermined material change with no documented assessment is also a fail.
testing.done: every breach shows recomputed day counts meeting the 1-day and 3-day clocks, or a logged fail.

testing.step: Walk through one breach (real or simulated) end to end
actions: If a real breach occurred, walk its full chain: alert → GRC record → CFO brief → determination → notice → action → recovery → CFO closure.
If none occurred, run a tabletop simulation with the Capital Management Manager and time each step against the protocol.
Record gaps between protocol and practice.
testing.done: one end-to-end walkthrough or simulation is documented with gaps recorded.

testing.step: Verify FCIC notification content and delivery
actions: For any notice sent, verify counsel clearance, CFO approval and delivery proof to the RMA contact named in the SRA.
Reconcile the quantified impact in the notice to the monitoring pack of record.
Confirm the same event appears consistently in the next quarterly RMA financial submission.
testing.done: each notice is cleared, approved, delivered with proof, and consistent with packs and RMA submissions.

testing.step: Verify governance reviews happened on schedule
actions: Check monthly review minutes exist for all twelve months and quarterly board packs for all four quarters.
Verify amber-metric actions carry owners, dates and closure evidence.
Verify the annual threshold review and metric validation were completed before July 1.
testing.done: all scheduled reviews, the threshold refresh and the metric validation are evidenced.

testing.step: Assess remediation closure quality
actions: For closed breach actions, verify the metric genuinely recovered above the trigger in the subsequent packs.
Verify CFO sign-off exists on each closure.
Reopen as exceptions any closure lacking recovery evidence.
testing.done: every closed breach shows metric recovery and CFO sign-off, or is reopened as an exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the month/breach, what failed and the SRA or RBC exposure.
Assign root cause (feed failure, silent alert, clock miss, missing determination) and an owner.
Set remediation dates; any missed FCIC notice triggers an immediate counsel assessment of corrective disclosure.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, and counsel assessment where notice was missed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare results to the zero-missed-pack and zero-late-escalation thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who prepares no packs and owns no breaches — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper and report to the board risk committee and Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to both committees.

checklist.step: Maintain the RMA filing calendar for the reinsurance year
actions: Enter every due date: Plan of Operations by April 1, quarterly financials within 45 days of each quarter end, annual audited financials per the SRA schedule, and the NAIC annual statement (March 1) as the upstream dependency.
Compute internal milestone dates backwards from each deadline (draft, review, certification, submission).
Arm T-60/T-30/T-10 alerts with the CFO office copied at T-10.
checklist.done: a complete calendar with back-scheduled milestones and armed alerts exists for the reinsurance year.

checklist.step: Prepare the Plan of Operations financial exhibits
actions: Build the exhibits per Appendix II: statutory surplus, projected MPCI premium by state and fund designation, retention plan and supporting schedules.
Take the projected premium and surplus-supported authorization from the Capital Management Manager's latest calc (C52).
Assemble the forms list and any required organizational/licensing attachments with the Product Filing Specialist.
checklist.done: a complete exhibit set derived from the capital calc and Appendix II requirements exists in draft.

checklist.step: Tie every exhibit figure to its source of record
actions: Tie surplus and balance-sheet figures to the filed NAIC annual statement pages and the SAP S/4HANA GL.
Tie premium projections to the capital workbook and eDAS-reported actuals for the current year.
Document each tie-out with preparer and date; clear every break before review.
checklist.done: every exhibit figure carries a documented tie-out to statement, GL or capital workbook with zero open breaks.

checklist.step: Run the internal review of the filing package
actions: Review exhibits against the Appendix II checklist and prior-year RMA comments.
Challenge the premium projection's consistency with the business plan and the requested authorization.
Record review comments and their clearance in the package.
checklist.done: a documented review with cleared comments exists before certification.

checklist.step: Obtain the CFO certification
actions: Review the final package and the tie-out summary.
Sign the certification/transmittal required for the Plan of Operations submission.
Return the signed package to the Regulatory Reporting Manager at least 5 business days before April 1.
checklist.done: a signed CFO certification exists with at least 5 business days of submission margin.

checklist.step: Submit the Plan of Operations by April 1 and capture the confirmation
actions: Log in to the RMA submission channel via USDA eAuthentication and upload the package to the Plan of Operations intake.
Capture the confirmation id and timestamp; where any component goes by transmittal letter, keep the date-stamped copy.
Record the submission date against the April 1 deadline in the tracker and file the as-filed package.
checklist.done: the package is submitted on or before April 1 with confirmation and the as-filed copy archived.

checklist.step: Prepare and submit the quarterly financial statements within 45 days
actions: Generate the quarterly statutory statement from the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) system after close.
Prepare the RMA quarterly submission with any Appendix II supplemental schedules.
Submit within 45 days of quarter end, capture the confirmation, and log the day count in the tracker.
checklist.done: each quarter's submission lands within 45 days with confirmation and day count logged.

checklist.step: File the annual audited financials on the SRA schedule
actions: Obtain the audited statutory financial statements and audit opinion from the Controller.
Submit to RMA per the SRA schedule and capture the confirmation.
Reconcile the audited figures to the previously filed quarterly submissions and note any differences for RMA questions.
checklist.done: the audited financials are filed on schedule with confirmation and a quarterly-reconciliation note.

checklist.step: Track FCIC approval of the Plan of Operations
actions: Monitor for FCIC's approval or deficiency notice ahead of the July 1 reinsurance year start.
Route any deficiency notice into the C50 objection process the day it arrives.
File the approval letter and any conditions in the archive (C51) and circulate conditions to the affected owners.
checklist.done: the FCIC approval (or an in-process deficiency response) is on file before July 1 with conditions circulated.

checklist.step: Answer RMA follow-up questions within 45 days
actions: Log each RMA question in the tracker with its 45-day due date computed from the written notice date.
Draft the response with tie-outs to the filed figures; obtain CFO approval for anything touching capital adequacy.
Submit through the channel RMA specifies and capture proof of submission.
checklist.done: every follow-up shows a logged due date, an approved response and submission proof within 45 days.

checklist.step: File amendments when filed information changes materially
actions: Assess material changes (premium projection, fund designations, financial condition) against the filed Plan of Operations with the Capital Management Manager.
Prepare and submit the amendment pages to RMA by the applicable deadline.
Link the amendment to the original filing in the tracker and archive.
checklist.done: material changes result in linked, submitted amendments rather than silent drift from the filed plan.

checklist.step: Cross-check filings against capital monitoring disclosures
actions: Before each submission, compare the figures to the latest capital monitoring pack (C53) and any FCIC notices sent.
Resolve any inconsistency before the filing goes out.
Document the cross-check in the filing package.
checklist.done: each filing carries a documented consistency check against monitoring packs and notices.

checklist.step: Archive every as-filed package with its confirmation
actions: File the as-filed package, certification, confirmation and correspondence under <reinsurance year>/RMA-financial-filings within 5 business days of submission.
Apply the retention label (3 years after crop year; approvals life-of-relationship plus 3).
Verify retrievability by filing type and due date.
checklist.done: every filing is archived with confirmation inside the 5-day SLA, labelled and retrievable.

checklist.step: Log filing exceptions with disposition
actions: Log any late filing, restated exhibit or missed follow-up with the day count and cause.
Notify the CFO the same day for any late statutory or Plan of Operations filing.
Record RMA's reaction and the corrective action taken.
checklist.done: every filing exception is logged with same-day CFO notice and a recorded corrective action.

checklist.step: Review the procedure annually against the current SRA
actions: Re-read the SRA reporting sections and Appendix II each year for changed deadlines or content requirements.
Fold in the April 1 cycle debrief points: milestone slippage, tie-out breaks and RMA comments.
Confirm the calendar template reflects any change before the new reinsurance year.
Sign and date the annual review.
checklist.done: a dated annual review confirms the calendar and procedure match the current SRA terms and absorb the cycle debrief.

testing.step: Build the population of required RMA filings for the year
actions: Derive the required-filing list independently from the 2026 SRA reporting terms: April 1 Plan of Operations, four quarterly submissions, annual audited financials, plus received follow-ups.
Compare to the company's filing calendar and list any requirement the calendar missed.
Sign the population as complete.
testing.done: an independently derived filing population is reconciled to the calendar and signed.

testing.step: Recompute timeliness for every filing
actions: Read the submission timestamp or date-stamped transmittal for each filing.
Recompute against the deadline: April 1, quarter end + 45 days, the SRA audited-financials date, and 45 days for each follow-up.
Any filing past its date is a fail regardless of RMA reaction.
testing.done: every filing has recomputed day-count maths and an on-time/late verdict.

testing.step: Trace submissions to confirmations
actions: Verify each filing holds a confirmation id, receipt or date-stamped transmittal in the archive.
Treat a filing without submission proof as unsubmitted — a fail, not a documentation gap.
Verify the FCIC approval of the Plan of Operations is on file before July 1.
testing.done: every filing traces to submission proof and the pre-July-1 approval is evidenced.

testing.step: Tie filed figures back to the statutory statement and GL
actions: For the Plan of Operations exhibits and two sampled quarterly submissions, re-tie surplus and premium figures to the statutory statement pages, the GL and the capital workbook.
Apply zero tolerance to tie-out differences.
Verify the requested premium authorization equals the capital calc's supported figure.
testing.done: sampled filed figures tie exactly to source, and the authorization request traces to the capital calc.

testing.step: Verify certification and review evidence
actions: Confirm the CFO certification is signed and dated before submission on the Plan of Operations.
Confirm the Statutory Reporting Manager's review comments and clearances exist for each sampled filing.
Flag any filing submitted without its required sign-offs.
testing.done: every sampled filing shows pre-submission certification and documented review.

testing.step: Sample RMA follow-ups and test the 45-day responses
actions: Select all follow-ups touching capital adequacy plus a random sample of others.
Recompute the 45-day clock from each written notice date to the response submission proof.
Verify CFO approval on capital-related responses and consistency with the filed figures.
testing.done: sampled follow-ups show on-time, approved, figure-consistent responses.

testing.step: Test amendment discipline
actions: Compare in-year material changes (from capital packs and board minutes) to the amendments actually filed.
Any material change to filed information with no amendment is an exception.
Verify amendments link to their originals in the tracker and archive.
testing.done: every material change traces to a filed, linked amendment or a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify archive completeness for the filing year
actions: Retrieve each population filing from the archive with certification, confirmation and correspondence.
Check filing-to-archive lag against the 5-business-day SLA.
Check retention labels.
testing.done: every filing is retrievable complete within SLA with correct retention labels.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the filing, deadline, day count and SRA exposure.
Assign root cause (calendar miss, close delay, certification bottleneck, channel confusion) and an owner.
Set remediation dates and carry open exceptions into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare results to the zero-late-filings and zero-tie-out-break thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who prepared and submitted nothing in the population — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper and report to the Compliance Committee and CFO.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
